title: Single-leaf protocols have zero complexity
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over input types $X$ and $Y$ with output type $\alpha$. If $p$ has exactly one leaf, that is, if the number of output nodes of $p$ equals $1$, then the communication complexity of $p$ is $0$.
hypotheses_covered: p is a deterministic communication protocol over X, Y, α
replaced:
If a protocol $p$ has exactly one leaf (i.e.\ $p.\mathrm{numLeaves} = 1$), then its
communication complexity satisfies $p.\mathrm{complexity} = 0$.
The only protocol with a single leaf is an immediate output node, which requires no
communication.
